mainTopic: The minimum measure of ראשית הגז, the one-in-sixty rule for ראשית הגז, תרומה and פאה, and the story of רבי יוחנן and איסי בר הִינִי.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: רבי יוחנן explains that רבי יוסי's view came from a tradition going back to חגי, זכריה and מלאכי. The גמרא then asks how much wool the רבנן's 'כל שהן' really means for ראשית הגז. רב, שמואל, רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר each give a different answer. A challenge from the משנה's 'five סלעים' is answered: five סלעים is the smallest gift for each כהן when someone has a lot of wool. The גמרא next examines רב ושמואל's rule that ראשית הגז, תרומה and פאה are one in sixty. It shows that for תרומה and פאה this is a rabbinic measure, and that for פאה it applies even outside ארץ ישראל. A story follows in which רבי יוחנן corrects איסי בר הִינִי's wording, rebukes him for calling רב by a casual nickname, and tells him the measure is sixty. Finally, רב דימי's report clears up apparent contradictions in רבי יוחנן's and רב's numbers. רב's 'מנה' turns out to be a large forty-סלע מנה, and the calculation finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's view came from a prophetic tradition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that רבי יוסי's opinion was accepted because he said it based on a tradition going back to the נביאים חגי, זכריה and מלאכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: He said it from a received tradition, from the mouth of חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes the earlier discussion. He explains why רבי יוסי's view was accepted: it was a tradition he had received, not just his own reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might have thought רבי יוסי's view was accepted because it was a nice middle position between other opinions. רבי יוחנן says no: it was a מסורה, a received tradition, going back to the last נביאים. A received tradition carries much more weight than a logical compromise.

keyTerms.meaning: From a received tradition (something heard and handed down)
A tradition passed down by teachers
He said it

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
He said it from a received tradition,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יוסי, whose opinion רבי accepted in the earlier discussion.

phrases.english: from the mouth of Chaggai, Zechariah, and Malachi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִפִּי שְׁמוּעָה אָמְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion that came before this section about why רבי יוסי's view was accepted.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי's view rests on a prophetic tradition from חגי, זכריה and מלאכי, not on compromise or logic.

steps.title: What does 'any amount' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's argument between רבי דוסא בן הרכינס and the רבנן. It asks how much wool the רבנן's phrase 'כל שהן' really refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא בן הרכינס says, etc. And how much is 'any amount'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by pointing back to a line in the משנה. It then asks a clarifying question about the רבנן's words 'כל שהן'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי דוסא gives a fixed weight for each sheep's wool, while the רבנן say 'any amount'. The גמרא asks whether 'any amount' really means even a tiny bit, or whether there is still some minimum. This question sets up the four answers that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.: a signal that the rest of the משנה's line is assumed
Any amount at all
And how much?
The first shearing of wool, given to the כהן

steps.confusionAlert: 'כל שהן' sounds like it must mean even the smallest amount, but the גמרא is asking exactly that. Most of the answers below say it still has a minimum. Only the רבנן's phrase is being explained here, not רבי דוסא's opinion.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי דּוֹסָא בֶּן הַרְכִּינָס אוֹמֵר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas says, etc.
phrases.notes: Back in the משנה, he requires each of the five sheep to give 150 dinars of wool. The רבנן say any amount.

phrases.english: And how much is 'any amount'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section, going back to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual minimum amount of wool behind the רבנן's phrase 'כל שהן'.

steps.title: רב: 150 dinars, split evenly among the five sheep
steps.stepSummary: רב says 'any amount' means a total of מנה ופרס (150 dinars), as long as it is divided evenly among the five sheep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: a מנה and a פרס, provided that they are divided into fives.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer. He says the minimum is 150 dinars of wool in total, split equally among five sheep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסא wanted 150 dinars from each sheep. According to רב, the רבנן need only 150 dinars in total, which is 30 per sheep. The condition מחומשות means each of the five sheep must contribute its share.

keyTerms.meaning: A weight of 100 dinars
Half a מנה, which is 50 dinars
Provided that
Divided into five equal parts

phrases.english: Rav said: a maneh and a peras,
phrases.notes: A מנה is 100 dinars and a פרס is half of that, so 150 dinars in total.

phrases.english: provided that they are divided into fives,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כל שהן' means 150 dinars in total, divided equally among five sheep.

steps.title: שמואל: sixty סלעים, with one סלע for the כהן
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the minimum is sixty סלעים of wool, and the owner gives one סלע of it to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: sixty, and he gives one סלע to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second answer. He says sixty סלעים in total, with one סלע going to the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's minimum is much larger than רב's. He also tells us how much the כהן gets: just one סלע out of sixty. That detail about the כהן's share will matter for the challenge in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: Sixty
A coin and unit of weight, equal to four dinars
He gives

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: sixty,
phrases.notes: He means sixty סלעים of wool in total.

phrases.english: and he gives one sela to the kohen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer from רב's to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A minimum of sixty סלעים, of which one סלע goes to the כהן.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: six סלעים, with five for the כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the minimum is six סלעים. Five go to the כהן and the owner keeps one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Six: five for the כהן, and one for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer is brought from רבי יוחנן. The minimum is six סלעים, and the כהן gets five of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's minimum is small, but it gives the כהן a large share: five out of six. He seems to set the minimum so that there is enough to give the כהן five סלעים and still leave something for the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Six
Five
And one for himself

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Six: five for the kohen, and one for himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שֵׁשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A minimum of six סלעים: five for the כהן and one for the owner.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: it literally means any amount
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the משנה's words 'כל שהן' mean exactly what they say: any amount, with no minimum.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: We learned 'any amount.'
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth answer is brought from רבי אלעזר. He says there is no hidden minimum, so even a tiny amount of wool is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the three earlier answers, רבי אלעזר reads the phrase plainly. Even a total of less than one סלע would require giving ראשית הגז. That means the כהן could receive very little.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Any amount' is what the משנה said, and it means just that

steps.whatToRemember: Four views on the רבנן's 'any amount': רב says 150 dinars split evenly among five sheep. שמואל says sixty סלעים, with one סלע to the כהן. רבי יוחנן says six סלעים, with five to the כהן. רבי אלעזר says truly any amount.

phrases.english: Ulla said in the name of Rabbi Elazar:
We learned 'any amount.'

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כׇּל שֶׁהֵן שָׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth answer, which rejects any minimum at all.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כל שהן' means literally any amount, with no minimum.

steps.title: The משנה's five סלעים challenges שמואל and רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, which says the כהן receives five סלעים by the יהודה measure. That fits רב and רבי יוחנן, but it contradicts שמואל and רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: And how much does he give him? The weight of five סלעים in יהודה, which are ten סלעים in the גליל. Granted, according to רב and רבי יוחנן, it works out well, but according to שמואל and רבי אלעזר, it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a line from the משנה about how much the כהן receives. It uses that line to challenge two of the four opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the כהן gets five סלעים of wool. רבי יוחנן said exactly that, and רב never discussed the כהן's share, so neither one is contradicted. But שמואל said the כהן gets only one סלע, and רבי אלעזר allows a total smaller than five סלעים, so both clash with the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The weight of
In יהודה, which used a heavier סלע
In the גליל, which used a lighter סלע (half the יהודה weight)
Granted, it is fine according to...
It works out well
It is difficult (a challenge)

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge leaves שמואל and רבי אלעזר needing a defense. Steps 8 and 9 answer it by reading the משנה differently.

phrases.english: We learned: And how much does he give him?
The weight of five sela'im in Yehuda,
which are ten sela'im in the Galil.
Granted, according to Rav and Rabbi Yochanan, it works out well,
but according to Shmuel and Rabbi Elazar, it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the four answers against the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinions of שמואל and רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires giving the כהן five סלעים. שמואל gives the כהן only one סלע, and רבי אלעזר allows a total below five סלעים, so both seem to contradict the משנה.

steps.title: Even רב does not fit the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: even רב has a problem with the משנה, because רב ושמואל both say ראשית הגז is one part in sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, does it work out for רב? But רב and שמואל both say: ראשית הגז is one part in sixty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge by showing that רב has the same problem as שמואל and רבי אלעזר. This sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says the minimum amount of wool is 150 dinars. If the כהן gets one-sixtieth of that, he gets only two and a half dinars, which is less than one סלע, and nowhere near five סלעים. So if the משנה's 'five סלעים' is a problem, it is a problem for רב too, and a different reading of the משנה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: turning the challenger's own logic back on him
Does it work out well?
The first shearing of wool, given to a כהן
One part in sixty

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
does it work out well for Rav?
But Rav and Shmuel both say:
The first shearing is one part in sixty!
phrases.notes: One-sixtieth of רב's 150 dinars is far less than five סלעים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Deflects the challenge of step 7 by showing that רב, whom the challenge assumed was safe, faces the same difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 7 that the משנה's 'five סלעים' supports רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב ושמואל say the כהן's share is one-sixtieth. One-sixtieth of רב's minimum of 150 dinars is less than one סלע, so רב cannot read the משנה as a required total of five סלעים either.

steps.title: Each כהן should get at least five סלעים
steps.stepSummary: רב ושמואל explain that the משנה is about someone with a lot of wool giving to several כהנים: each כהן should receive no less than five סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was already stated about that משנה: רב and שמואל both say, we are dealing with a Jew who has a lot of shearings and wants to give them to the כהן. We tell him: do not give any one כהן less than five סלעים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the משנה's 'five סלעים' is not the minimum total of wool. It is the smallest gift any single כהן should receive when there is plenty of wool to give.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the משנה is no longer a problem for anyone. The one-in-sixty rule decides the total gift, and 'five סלעים' only tells a person with a large amount of wool not to split it into gifts that are too small. This removes the challenge of step 7 against שמואל and רבי אלעזר as well.

keyTerms.meaning: We are dealing with (this case)
Shearings, the cut wool
Do not give less
סלעים, a weight or coin unit

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'five סלעים' is the minimum gift for each כהן when the owner has a lot of wool. It is not the minimum amount of wool that creates the obligation.

phrases.english: It was already stated about that one,
phrases.notes: 'That one' means the משנה that mentioned five סלעים.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel both say:

phrases.aramaic: בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ גִּיזִּין הַרְבֵּה עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: We are dealing with a Jew who has many shearings,
and he wants to give them to the Kohen,
and we say to him:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל חַד וְחַד לָא תְּבַצַּר לֵיהּ
phrases.english: to each and every one, do not give him less
than five sela'im.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty raised in steps 7 and 8 by reading the משנה as a case of distributing a large amount of wool.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the משנה (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's five סלעים is the required total, which would conflict with the one-in-sixty rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The five סלעים is the minimum gift for each כהן when a person with a lot of wool gives it out. The total is still one in sixty.

steps.title: רב ושמואל: ראשית הגז, תרומה and פאה are one in sixty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the statement of רב ושמואל and quotes it in full: ראשית הגז, תרומה and פאה are each one part in sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself: רב and שמואל both say, ראשית הגז is one in sixty, תרומה is one in sixty, and פאה is one in sixty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now studies the statement of רב ושמואל that it quoted a moment ago, and gives its full wording. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, only the ראשית הגז part was quoted. The full statement says the same one-in-sixty measure also applies to תרומה and to פאה, and the next step will challenge the תרומה part.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: returning to study a statement that was quoted in passing
The portion of produce given to a כהן
The corner of the field left for the poor

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Rav and Shmuel both say:
The first shearing is one in sixty,
terumah is one in sixty, pe'ah is one in sixty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the statement quoted in step 8 and examines it on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראשית הגז, תרומה and פאה are each measured at one part in sixty.

steps.title: But a משנה says תרומה is one in forty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the תרומה part: a משנה says that a generous person gives one-fortieth as תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is תרומה one in sixty? But we learned in a משנה: for תרומה, a generous person gives one out of forty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב ושמואל's statement that תרומה is one in sixty. It quotes a משנה that gives a different number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה about תרומה names one-fortieth as the amount a generous person gives. That seems to clash with רב ושמואל's one in sixty.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'a good eye': a generous person
One out of forty

phrases.english: Terumah is one in sixty?
But we learned in a Mishnah:
Terumah, a generous eye: one out of forty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תרומה part of the statement quoted in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ושמואל's statement that תרומה is one in sixty.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה names one-fortieth as the measure of תרומה for a generous person, which does not match one in sixty.

steps.title: One in sixty by Torah law, one in forty by rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one in sixty is the דאורייתא measure, while one in forty is the דרבנן measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: By Torah law, it is one in sixty. By rabbinic law, it is one in forty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the challenge by showing that the two numbers belong to two different levels of law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ושמואל were speaking about the Torah-level measure, one in sixty. The משנה's one in forty is the higher measure set by the רבנן. Since they are not talking about the same level, there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
By rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the גמרא splits the two numbers: one in sixty as the Torah level and one in forty as the rabbinic level. The very next step challenges this, and step 14 replaces it.

phrases.english: By Torah law: one in sixty,
by rabbinic law: one in forty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 11 by splitting the two numbers between Torah law and rabbinic law.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing levels of law (דאורייתא versus דרבנן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The one-in-sixty statement and the one-in-forty משנה give conflicting measures for the same obligation.
steps.terutzMaskana: One in sixty is the Torah measure, and one in forty is the rabbinic measure, so both are correct.

steps.title: Is one in sixty really the Torah measure for תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last answer: שמואל himself says that by דאורייתא even one grain of wheat exempts a whole pile.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the דאורייתא measure really one in sixty? But שמואל said: one grain of wheat exempts the whole pile!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 12, which said that one in sixty is the דאורייתא measure of תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל taught that by דאורייתא there is no minimum at all: a single grain set aside as תרומה frees the whole pile. If that is true, one in sixty cannot be the דאורייתא measure.

keyTerms.meaning: One single grain of wheat
Exempts, frees from the obligation
A pile of harvested grain

phrases.english: By Torah law it is one in sixty?
But didn't Shmuel say:
One grain of wheat exempts the whole pile!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that one in sixty is the דאורייתא measure of תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל says that by דאורייתא one grain is enough, so there is no fixed Torah measure of one in sixty.

steps.title: Three levels of the תרומה measure
steps.stepSummary: By דאורייתא one grain is enough. By דרבנן, produce that the Torah obligates needs one in forty, and produce obligated only by the רבנן needs one in sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: By Torah law, it is like שמואל said (one grain). By rabbinic law, for produce obligated by Torah law, it is one in forty. By rabbinic law, for produce obligated only by rabbinic law, it is one in sixty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes its earlier answer and sets out three separate levels for the amount of תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 had called one in sixty דאורייתא. Now the גמרא says that both forty and sixty are דרבנן, and the Torah itself requires only one grain. The רבנן asked for more (one in forty) when the obligation itself comes from the Torah. They asked for less (one in sixty) when the whole obligation is only דרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic amount, for produce that the Torah obligates
A rabbinic amount, for produce obligated only by the רבנן
One part out of forty

steps.confusionAlert: Don't hold on to step 12's answer. The גמרא has now replaced it: one in sixty is NOT דאורייתא. It is the rabbinic amount for produce that is only rabbinically obligated.

phrases.english: By Torah law – it is like Shmuel said,
By rabbinic law, for produce obligated by Torah law – one in forty,
By rabbinic law, for produce obligated by rabbinic law – one in sixty.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא – כְּדִשְׁמוּאֵל, דְּרַבָּנַן בִּדְאוֹרָיְיתָא – אַחַת מֵאַרְבָּעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases into levels (Torah vs. rabbinic, and type of produce)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One in sixty is the דאורייתא measure of תרומה
steps.terutzMaskana: דאורייתא needs only one grain. One in forty is דרבנן for Torah-obligated produce, and one in sixty is דרבנן for rabbinically obligated produce.

steps.title: But פאה has no measure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the פאה part of רב ושמואל's statement from a משנה that lists פאה among things with no fixed measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: פאה is one in sixty? But we learned in a משנה: these are the things that have no fixed measure: פאה, ביכורים, and the ראיון offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in רב ושמואל's list, פאה, and attacks it from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ושמואל gave פאה a measure of one in sixty. The משנה at the start of מסכת פאה says outright that פאה has no measure, so the two sources seem to contradict.

keyTerms.meaning: The corner of the field left for the poor
A fixed measure or amount
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש
The offering brought when 'appearing' at the בית המקדש on the festivals

phrases.english: Pe'a is one in sixty?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
These are the things that have no fixed measure:
Pe'a, and the first fruits, and the appearance offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תרומה part of רב ושמואל's statement to the פאה part
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ושמואל's claim that פאה is one in sixty
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה explicitly says פאה has no fixed measure.

steps.title: No Torah measure, but a rabbinic one
steps.stepSummary: By דאורייתא פאה has no measure. The one in sixty of רב ושמואל is a דרבנן measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: By Torah law it has no measure; by rabbinic law it is one in sixty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה and רב ושמואל are talking about two different levels of law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes the Torah law: even a tiny amount of פאה fulfills the מצוה. רב ושמואל describe what the רבנן added: a minimum of one in sixty.

keyTerms.meaning: It has no fixed amount

phrases.english: By Torah law – it has no measure,
By rabbinic law – it is one in sixty.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא – אֵין לָהּ שִׁיעוּר, דְּרַבָּנַן – בְּשִׁשִּׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting Torah law from rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ושמואל's one in sixty contradicts the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks about דאורייתא, and רב ושמואל speak about דרבנן.

steps.title: What did רב ושמואל add?
steps.stepSummary: If one in sixty is the rabbinic measure, a משנה already teaches this, so why did רב ושמואל need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this teaching us? We already learned it: one may not give less than one in sixty for פאה, even though they said פאה has no measure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the opposite question: רב ושמואל's statement looks unnecessary, because a משנה already says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The very next משנה in מסכת פאה says that you should not give less than one in sixty, even though פאה has no Torah measure. That is exactly the answer of step 16, so רב ושמואל seem to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: What new thing is this teaching us?
One may not give less than

phrases.english: What is this teaching us?
We already learned it:
One may not give less than one in sixty for pe'a,
even though they said
that pe'a has no measure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 16's answer, the statement of רב ושמואל now seems unnecessary
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רב ושמואל's statement about פאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already teaches the rabbinic one-in-sixty rule, so the statement adds nothing.

steps.title: ארץ ישראל versus חוצה לארץ
steps.stepSummary: The משנה speaks about פאה in ארץ ישראל. רב ושמואל teach that the same one in sixty applies in חוצה לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about the Land of Israel; here, it is talking about outside the Land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב ושמואל are teaching something new: where their rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule of one in sixty is about fields in ארץ ישראל. רב ושמואל add that the same one-in-sixty measure applies to פאה outside the Land too.

keyTerms.meaning: In ארץ ישראל
Outside ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: For תרומה and פאה, רב ושמואל's 'one in sixty' is not the Torah measure. For תרומה, the Torah needs only one grain. For פאה, the Torah has no measure. Their statement about פאה adds that the rabbinic minimum applies even in חוצה לארץ.

phrases.english: There, it is in the Land of Israel,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the משנה in מסכת פאה.

phrases.english: here, it is outside the Land.
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the statement of רב ושמואל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ושמואל only repeat the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: רב ושמואל extend the one-in-sixty rule of פאה to חוצה לארץ.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן corrects a word in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן finds איסי בר הִינִי teaching his son the word רחלים in our משנה, and tells him to say רחלות instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: When איסי בר הִינִי went up to ארץ ישראל, רבי יוחנן found him teaching his son 'רחלים.' He said to him: Teach him 'רחלות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new short story about the exact wording used for 'sheep' in our משנה of ראשית הגז. This sets up the back-and-forth that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איסי was using רחלים, the masculine-looking plural of רחל (sheep). רבי יוחנן wants the feminine plural form רחלות, which is how the language of the משנה says it.

keyTerms.meaning: Went up (to ארץ ישראל from בבל)
Teaches (a משנה to a student)
Two plural forms of 'sheep'

phrases.english: When Isi bar Hini went up,
phrases.notes: He came up from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan found him
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Either way, רבי יוחנן found איסי.

phrases.english: teaching his son "reḥelim" (sheep),
He said to him: Teach him "reḥelot."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the wording of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה should say רחלות, not רחלים.

steps.title: איסי brings a פסוק for his wording
steps.stepSummary: איסי defends רחלים by pointing to the פסוק 'רחלים מאתים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: As it is written, 'two hundred רחלים.'
steps.whatsHappening: איסי pushes back on רבי יוחנן's correction using a word from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה itself uses the form רחלים, so איסי argues that this must be the correct form to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (in a פסוק)

phrases.english: He said to him: As it is written: "Two hundred reḥelim."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's correction
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's instruction to say רחלות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק uses רחלים, so that form should be correct.

steps.title: The language of the תורה and the language of חכמים are separate
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the תורה's language and the language of חכמים are each their own, so the משנה uses רחלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The language of the תורה is its own, and the language of חכמים is its own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains why a word from a פסוק does not decide how the משנה should be worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לשון תורה and לשון חכמים work like two separate styles of Hebrew. The משנה is written in לשון חכמים, so it uses רחלות even though the פסוק says רחלים.

keyTerms.meaning: The Hebrew of the תורה
The Hebrew of חכמים, such as in the משנה
On its own, separate

steps.whatToRemember: לשון תורה לעצמה, לשון חכמים לעצמן: you cannot fix the wording of a משנה just by copying the wording of a פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule for reading the משנה: its Hebrew has its own forms and should be read on its own terms.

phrases.english: He said to him: The language of the Torah is its own,
and the language of the Sages is its own.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְשׁוֹן תּוֹרָה לְעַצְמָהּ, לְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים לְעַצְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers איסי's challenge in step 20
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק's word רחלים should be used in the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows לשון חכמים, so it says רחלות.

steps.title: Who heads the yeshiva in בבל?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks איסי who is the head of the yeshiva in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Who is the head of the yeshiva in בבל?
steps.whatsHappening: Still talking with איסי, רבי יוחנן asks a simple question: who is the leading teacher in בבל? This sets up the next exchange.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real information question, not a challenge. Its purpose is to bring up רב, which leads to רבי יוחנן's strong reaction.

keyTerms.meaning: Head of the study session, the leading teacher of a yeshiva
Babylonia, the great Torah center outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is speaking to איסי, the same איסי from the רחלים/רחלות exchange.

phrases.english: Who is the head of the yeshiva in Bavel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the conversation between רבי יוחנן and איסי that began in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who the head of the yeshiva in בבל is.

steps.title: איסי answers: אבא אריכא
steps.stepSummary: איסי answers that it is 'אבא אריכא', meaning רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Abba the tall.
steps.whatsHappening: איסי answers by calling רב by a casual nickname, 'tall אבא'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer itself is correct, since רב was the head of the yeshiva. The trouble is how איסי says it: he uses a familiar nickname for a giant of Torah, and that sets up רבי יוחנן's rebuke.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Tall אבא', a nickname for רב, whose name was אבא

phrases.english: He said to him: Abba the tall.
phrases.notes: רב's actual name was אבא; 'the tall' is a nickname, so he means רב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The head of the yeshiva is רב, whom איסי calls 'אבא אריכא'.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן scolds איסי and describes רב's greatness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן objects to the casual nickname. He remembers sitting seventeen rows behind רב while 'sparks of fire' passed between רב and רבי, and he could not follow what they said.
steps.simpleTranslation: You call him 'Abba the tall'?! I remember sitting seventeen rows behind רב, who sat before רבי. Sparks of fire went from רב's mouth to רבי's mouth and from רבי's mouth to רב's mouth, and I did not understand what they were saying. And you call him 'Abba the tall'?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן is upset that איסי speaks about רב so casually. He explains how great רב was in his own memory.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן was himself a great sage, yet as a young student he could not follow the back-and-forth between רב and רבי. The 'sparks of fire' describe how sharp and deep their learning was. His point is that someone that great deserves to be spoken of with respect.

keyTerms.meaning: Rows of students sitting in the study hall
Sparks of fire, a picture of brilliant, intense Torah discussion

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches respect for Torah giants and shows that even a great sage like רבי יוחנן stood in awe of רב.

phrases.english: He said to him:
You call him "Abba the tall"?!
I remember when I was sitting
seventeen rows back
behind Rav, who sat before Rabbi,
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no other name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: and sparks of fire came out
from the mouth of Rav to the mouth of Rabbi,
and from the mouth of Rabbi to the mouth of Rav,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵית אֲנָא יָדַע מָה הֵן אָמְרִין,
phrases.english: and I did not know what they were saying,
and you call him "Abba the tall"?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the casual nickname איסי used in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב was so great that even רבי יוחנן could not follow his discussions with רבי, so he must be spoken of with respect.

steps.title: איסי asks the minimum amount for ראשית הגז
steps.stepSummary: איסי asks how much wool must be sheared before the מצוה of ראשית הגז applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (איסי) said to him: The first shearing, at how much?
steps.whatsHappening: Now איסי asks רבי יוחנן a halachic question: what is the minimum amount of shorn wool for ראשית הגז?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new halachic topic in the conversation. The question is about a minimum measure, the same kind of question the earlier steps discussed.

keyTerms.meaning: The first shearing: a portion of sheep's wool given to a כהן
At how much, asking for the minimum amount

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: 'He' here is איסי, now asking רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: The first shearing, at how much?
phrases.notes: He means: how much wool must be sheared before you are obligated to give a portion to the כהן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the story about רב to a halachic question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum amount of shorn wool that creates the obligation of ראשית הגז.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: sixty
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the obligation starts at sixty (סלעים).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: At sixty.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a clear number: sixty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He sets a real minimum, sixty סלעים in weight of wool. This sounds different from the plain words of the משנה, and איסי is about to point that out.

keyTerms.meaning: At sixty, meaning sixty סלעים in weight

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him: At sixty.
phrases.notes: Sixty סלעים of wool by weight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers איסי's question from step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ראשית הגז applies once sixty סלעים of wool are sheared.

steps.title: But the משנה says 'any amount'
steps.stepSummary: איסי challenges him: the משנה says ראשית הגז applies to any amount of wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: 'any amount'!
steps.whatsHappening: איסי pushes back. Our משנה seems to say there is no minimum at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge sets רבי יוחנן's number, sixty, against the plain words of the משנה, 'any amount'. If the משנה has no minimum, where does sixty come from?

keyTerms.meaning: At any amount at all, with no minimum

phrases.english: But we learned "at any amount"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's answer in step 26.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says 'any amount', which seems to rule out any minimum like sixty.

steps.title: If so, what's the difference between us?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers: if the plain משנה were enough, what would be the difference between my knowledge and yours?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, what is the difference between me and you?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that the halacha is not always clear from simply reading the משנה. A scholar knows the final ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not deny that the משנה says 'any amount'. His point is that he knows the accepted halacha, sixty, while איסי knows only the משנה's surface wording. That deeper knowledge is what sets a great scholar apart.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if what you say were true
What is the difference between me and you?

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not throwing out the משנה. He is saying the practical halacha (sixty) is known through deeper learning beyond the simple wording.

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
what is the difference between me and you?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, מָה בֵּין לִי וְלָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers איסי's challenge from step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to known halachic tradition beyond the plain משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'any amount' means there is no minimum.
steps.terutzMaskana: The accepted halacha, known to the scholar, is sixty, even though the משנה reads 'any amount'.

steps.title: רב דימי reports: רב sixty, רבי ינאי six
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that for ראשית הגז, רב says sixty, while רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי ינאי, says six.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: For the first shearing, רב says sixty, and רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי ינאי says six.
steps.whatsHappening: A new report arrives with רב דימי. It gives two opinions on the minimum for ראשית הגז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the number six is said by רבי יוחנן, but in the name of his teacher רבי ינאי. This detail matters for the next steps, because רבי יוחנן himself told איסי sixty.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came, used for sages who brought teachings from ארץ ישראל to בבל
In the name of, quoting someone else
At six (סלעים)

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
The first shearing: Rav says at sixty,
and Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Yannai
says at six.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new report on the same measure רבי יוחנן gave איסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: ראשית הגז applies at sixty. רבי ינאי (quoted by רבי יוחנן): at six.

steps.title: אביי: you fixed one problem and made another
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רב דימי that his report solves one difficulty but creates a new one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב דימי: You settled one thing for us, and you made one thing difficult for us.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי reacts to the report with a two-part comment. This line sets up the next steps, which explain each part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The report fixes one contradiction and raises another. The גמרא first explains what was fixed (next step), and the difficulty comes after that.

keyTerms.meaning: You settled one thing for us
You made one thing difficult for us

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Dimi:

phrases.aramaic: אַנַּחְתְּ לַן חֲדָא וְאַקְשֵׁת לַן חֲדָא.
phrases.english: You settled one thing for us and made one thing difficult for us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַנַּחְתְּ לַן חֲדָא וְאַקְשֵׁת לַן חֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב דימי's report in step 29.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The report resolves one contradiction but creates another, which is explained next.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן vs. רבי יוחנן is settled
steps.stepSummary: The part that is settled: the six and the sixty tied to רבי יוחנן do not contradict. Sixty is his own view, and six is his teacher רבי ינאי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, רבי יוחנן against רבי יוחנן is not difficult: this one is his own view, and that one is his teacher's.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains the 'settled' half. רבי יוחנן's two numbers no longer clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, six (step 5) and sixty (step 26) both seemed to come from רבי יוחנן, which looked like a contradiction. רב דימי's report shows that the six was only רבי יוחנן quoting רבי ינאי, while his own view is sixty, as he told איסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part is fine (a 'but' usually follows)
It is not difficult
This is his own view, that is his teacher's

phrases.english: Granted, Rabbi Yochanan against Rabbi Yochanan
is not difficult:
this is his own, that is his teacher's.
phrases.notes: Sixty is רבי יוחנן's own view; six is what he reported from his teacher, רבי ינאי.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the 'settled one thing' half of אביי's comment in step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the statements between a sage and his teacher
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן said both six and sixty, which contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sixty is רבי יוחנן's own view; six is רבי ינאי's view, which he only reported.

steps.title: רב's two amounts seem to clash
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the new problem אביי pointed to. רב said 'a מנה and a half,' but רב דימי reported that רב says sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one statement of רב against another statement of רב is a difficulty, because רב said: a מנה and a half!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out the new difficulty that אביי mentioned. רב seems to contradict himself about the minimum amount of wool for ראשית הגז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי reported that רב requires sixty סלעים of wool. But רב is also quoted as saying 'a מנה and a half.' A regular מנה is 100 דינרים, so a מנה and a half is only 150 דינרים, which is much less than sixty סלעים (240 דינרים).

keyTerms.meaning: One statement of רב against another statement of רב (a self-contradiction)
A unit of money or weight, usually 100 דינרים
Half (here, half a מנה)
The first shearing of wool, which must be given to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Sixty here means sixty סלעים, and a סלע is 4 דינרים. That is why sixty סלעים (240 דינרים) seems far more than a regular מנה and a half (150 דינרים).

phrases.english: But the statement of רב against the statement of רב is a difficulty,
for רב said: a מנה and a half!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 31 settled the contradiction in רבי יוחנן's statements. This step states the remaining contradiction, in רב's statements.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's report that רב requires sixty
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב elsewhere says a מנה and a half, which is far less than sixty סלעים, so רב appears to contradict himself.

steps.title: רב's מנה is a larger forty-סלע מנה
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction goes away because רב's 'מנה' is a special large מנה worth forty סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The contradiction between רב and רב is also not difficult. What is the מנה he spoke of? A מנה of forty סלעים, which comes out to…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by explaining what size מנה רב meant. The sentence continues past this point, where the גמרא finishes the calculation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב did not mean a regular מנה of 100 דינרים (25 סלעים). He meant a bigger מנה of forty סלעים. A מנה and a half of that kind is forty plus twenty, which equals sixty סלעים. That matches רב דימי's report exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Is also not a difficulty
A coin or weight equal to 4 דינרים
A large מנה worth forty סלעים (160 דינרים)

steps.whatToRemember: Both contradictions are now resolved. רבי יוחנן's sixty is his own view, and רבי ינאי's six is his teacher's view. רב's 'מנה and a half' uses a forty-סלע מנה, which equals sixty סלעים.

phrases.english: The statement of רב against the statement of רב is also not difficult,
What is the מנה that he spoke of?
One of forty סלעים, which comes out to be…

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term: the 'מנה' is a larger unit than usual
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's מנה was thought to be a regular 100-דינר מנה, which totals less than sixty סלעים.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's מנה is forty סלעים, so a מנה and a half equals sixty סלעים, matching רב דימי's report.
